features.summary: The Orders page (/orders) is the staff queue for B2B and B2C orders: a server-paged list with tabs (Open, Needs review, Queued, Processing, Completed, Rejected, All), toolbar filters, per-tab counts read from x-total-count, a CSV export and a drawer per order (detail, timeline, ledger trail, pricing snapshot). The drawer and bulk bar run every order action (accept, reply, reject, reopen, refund, verification, notes, dispatch, fetch, change-supplier) and the paste-based bulk reply. The same list is embedded on merchant/customer pages (fixed clientId/customerId), in the command palette and in the supplier reroute dialog.

endpoints.request: Never fetched: the console renders a plain link `<a href=API_BASE/admin/files/:id target=_blank>` (orders.ts:63, OrderResult.tsx:26-31, OrderDetails.tsx:30), so the browser sends only the session cookie (no X-CSRF-Token, no Accept: application/json). :id is orders.input_file_id (`inputFileId`) or orders.result_file_id (`result.fileId`); merchants' KYC document links use the same route (M47).
endpoints.response: 302 with Location = short-lived presigned object-storage URL (Content-Disposition attachment; filename from files.filename). Any error is rendered raw in the new tab, so keep `detail` readable. Proposal: audit-log the access (files hold personal data).

errors.ui: raw error page in the new tab
links are hidden without files:read; raw page if reached
raw page in the new tab

endpoints.query: Simple-rest. `_start`/`_end`: 25 per page; tab and past-SLA counts use `_start=0&_end=1` (8 calls every 30 s, useOrderCounts.ts:20-31); palette `_end=5&_sort=createdAt&_order=desc` (paletteSource.ts:18-21); supplier reroute `_end=200&_sort=createdAt&_order=asc&supplierId=X&status=pending&status=processing` (useSupplierOrders.ts:16-24). `_sort` is only createdAt | totalPrice | status (filters.ts:89); queue tabs default createdAt asc, others desc (filters.ts:99). Filters, repeated key = IN: `status` (pending|processing|completed|rejected), `queue` (pending|manual|needs_attention|verification|review), `type` (service type imei|server|remote|file), `supplierId`, `clientId` (merchant page), `customerId` (customer page), `channel` (b2b|b2c), `pastSla=true` (pastSla=true = open (status pending|processing) and orders.placed_at < now() - make_interval(mins => services.sla_minutes), one age-only predicate with no queue exclusion (B92), shared with the dashboard and GET /admin/system/orders-health; placed_at equals created_at because placement never sets either explicitly (a contract test checks it on every placement path); a service with a null or 0 SLA is never past SLA; queue and status filters combine with it by AND, so System health's link queue=needs_attention&pastSla=true lists rows (M230)). Tabs: Open = status pending+processing; Needs review = queue manual+needs_attention+verification+review; Queued = queue pending; Processing/Completed/Rejected = status (status.ts:89-106). `q`: case-insensitive contains over id, imei, supplier_ref, client name, customer name, service name (mock handlers/orders.ts:15); the console strips ORD-/SF-/# so a numeric q must match the order id exactly (filters.ts:141).
endpoints.response: JSON array + `x-total-count` (total before paging, CORS-exposed). Row = orders columns plus derived fields: `status` Dhru word; `queue` derived (see businessRules) or null; `reviewReason` readable text or null; `channel` b2b when client_id is set, b2c when customer_id is set; `source` dhru|v1|portal|store|admin (status.ts:129-138); `service` {id, name, type, slaMinutes, category name}; `client` {id,name} or null; `customer` {id,name,email} with the full email (masked in the browser, BuyerCell.tsx:15) or null; `supplier` {id,name} or null; `supplierRef`; `attempts` (supplier send attempts); `result` {code: result_code, comment: result_comment, fileId: result_file_id}; money (unitPrice, totalPrice, unitCost, totalCost, taxAmount) as 4-dp USD strings, totalPrice net of VAT (gross = totalPrice + taxAmount, lib/money.ts:13-16); `currency` = buyer display currency (USD for B2B, checkout currency for B2C) with `pricingSnapshot.fx` (USD to that currency) and `pricingSnapshot.taxRate` as a fraction (lib/money.ts:18-28, OrderMoney.tsx:70-73); `completedAt` set for both completed and rejected (SlaCell). `dispatchState` is passed through but unused by screens. imei is always a string: orders.imei holds the order's main input, written at placement by one shared orders helper used by every placement path (Dhru, REST v1, portal, admin, store): type imei = the IMEI; server and remote = the value of the service's first required service_field by sort (for example username, serial, account); file = the first field value if the service has fields, else the uploaded file's original name. The column stays nullable (anonymisation erases it to NULL; a service with no input leaves it NULL) and the read model sends COALESCE(imei, '').

endpoints.response: Bare JSON array of every order_events row of the order (no paging, no x-total-count); any order, the console sorts oldest first. Event = {id, type (CHECK order_events_type_check, the console's words: created for placement (not 'placed'), hold, dispatch (sent to supplier), ack (REFERENCEID received), accepted, completed, settle, rejected, release, refund, retry (staff dispatch), review (a queue opened, data.reason), reopened, supplier_changed, verification, note, paid, risk, notify, dispute, and fetch; a new type later needs a migration), fromStatus|null, toStatus|null, actor {type staff|client|customer|system|supplier, id|null, name|null}, data, createdAt}. `data.message` is shown verbatim when present; otherwise the console words these types from data fields: created(source), hold, dispatch(supplier), ack(ref), accepted, completed, settle, rejected(reason), release, refund(reason), retry, review(reason), reopened(reason), supplier_changed, verification(decision), note(body), paid, risk, notify, dispute; an `order.`/`order_` prefix is tolerated (lib/events.ts:9-60). actor.name is joined (staff, merchant, customer or supplier name). Internal notes appear here but must never reach client/store/v1 timelines. A fetch that finds the order still running writes type 'fetch' with data.message 'Supplier has not finished yet'.
endpoints.mapConflict: order_events.actor_id is polymorphic over staff_users, clients and customers only; the console also expects actor types `system` (id null) and `supplier`. Proposal: allow actor_type supplier (actor_id = suppliers.id) and system (null).

endpoints.query: Same filters, `q`, `_sort` and `_order` as GET /admin/orders; `_start`/`_end` are never sent (useOrderExport.ts:15, orders.test.ts:312-316): export every matching row.
endpoints.request: Sent with Accept: */* and credentials; downloaded as a blob.
endpoints.response: text/csv body with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=...` (the console uses that name, else `orders-<tab>.csv`; the header must be listed in Access-Control-Expose-Headers). Mock columns: id,created,channel,buyer,service,input,status,supplier,price,cost (handlers/orders.ts:74-91). The toast says 'Exported N orders' with the list total, so include all matching rows. Stream it; the matching rows are counted first and more than 100000 is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with detail 'Too many rows (N); narrow the filters (max 100000)'; every export writes audit_logs.

endpoints.response: 204, no body (console refetches order, events and counts). Manual order (status pending, dispatch_state manual) moves to status processing with queue null (orders.test.ts expects {status: processing, queue: null}); order_events `accepted` (actor staff); audit_logs; outbox order.status_changed (STATUS 1). endpoints.request: Body `{ supplierId?, resetReference?, dispatch? }`. supplierId omitted keeps the current supplier and supplier service and applies only resetReference (supplier_ref = NULL); neither supplierId nor resetReference: true is 422 errors[{field: supplierId}] 'Choose a supplier or reset the reference'; the same supplier without a reset is a 204 with no event. The console always sends `{ supplierId, resetReference: true }` and then calls dispatch (drawer reroute useOrderMutations.ts:169-183, bulk useBulkSend.ts:20-35, supplier Reroute dialog). supplierId is a SUPPLIER id: the server must resolve orders.supplier_service_id from the order service's service_supplier_links whose supplier_services.supplier_id = supplierId (active link, lowest priority). resetReference=true clears supplier_ref so the next dispatch places a new supplier order.
endpoints.response: 204. Does not contact the supplier (map). order_events `supplier_changed` (data {fromSupplierId, toSupplierId, resetReference, costAbovePrice: true|false}, so the loss shows in reports), audit_logs. The server refreshes unit_cost = credit x credit_rate (4 dp USD) and total_cost = unit_cost x quantity from the chosen link (price unchanged); the B117(6) failover limit applies to automatic failover only, so a staff change to a costlier link is allowed and the event records costAbovePrice. dispatch_state stays as it is, except sent + resetReference becomes needs_attention (reason 'Supplier changed: dispatch needed'); with dispatch: true it becomes pending and the job is enqueued in the same transaction. If the following dispatch fails, the move stands (useBulkSend.ts:26-34), so the order must stay dispatchable.

Force-send to the order's supplier service (dispatch_state from needs_attention, manual or operator to pending; an order already pending answers 204 as a no-op because it is queued; no B117(6) check on a staff dispatch, the order goes to its chosen supplier service as is): dispatch_state pending and a `supplier-dispatch` job (decision 020), attempts +1, order_events `retry`/`dispatch`, supplier_api_logs row; on REFERENCEID the worker stores supplier_ref and sets status processing (STATUS 1). No money moves (hold stays). Map timeout step 10: staff dispatch only after checking the supplier did not run it; never auto-resend. The console toast says 'Status is now Processing' and refetches.

endpoints.response: 204. Calls getimeiorder for supplier_ref now (supplier_api_logs row). STATUS 4: complete the order (result_code, ledger complete); STATUS 3: reject (ledger reject); still running: order_events `fetch` with data.message 'Supplier has not finished yet', and dispatch_state needs_attention becomes sent once the supplier confirms it has the order. dispatch_state: STATUS 4 gives done + completed, STATUS 3 gives done + rejected. endpoints.request: Body `{ body }` (trimmed, required; the form caps it at 500 chars, OrderNoteForm.tsx:34).
endpoints.response: 204. Appends order_events `note` (data.body, actor staff) and sets orders.admin_note to the latest note (drawer 'Internal note'). Any status. Never exposed to buyers or webhooks.

endpoints.response: 204. Completed B2B order only, reopen + reject in one DB transaction: status rejected, result_code = reason, completed_at = now; ledger revenue to client_hold to client_wallet (net revenue to client_wallet, total_price); cogs is NOT reversed (UI: 'A refund after delivery loses the supplier cost', OrderFooter.tsx:140-141); order_events rejected + refund (data.reason); webhook STATUS 3; audit. The drawer's money trail reads GET /admin/ledger/transactions?refType=order&refId=<id> (mock kind `refund`). dispatch_state stays done, status rejected.

endpoints.request: Body `{ reason }`: a preset (lib/reply.ts:51-58) or typed text up to 120 chars (RejectDialog.tsx:114); buyer-visible. Bulk reject = one call per order, sequential, same reason (useBulkReject.ts).
endpoints.response: 204. Open order (pending|processing) becomes rejected; result_code = reason; completed_at = now; a not-yet-sent outbox dispatch is cancelled; a reserved inventory code returns to available. B2B: ledger reject client_hold to client_wallet (total_price), events rejected + release. B2C: full refund before delivery as map scenario b2c-refund: refunds row (method original, gross amount), ledger customer_funds to gateway_clearing (net) + vat_payable to gateway_clearing (tax), gateway refund, events rejected + refund. Webhook STATUS 3; audit. dispatch_state becomes done (any open order that is not held), status rejected.

endpoints.request: Body `{ reason? }` (optional, up to 140 chars, ReopenDialog.tsx:39); the console sends `{}` when empty. Permission orders:reopen.
endpoints.response: 204. Completed order goes back to processing; completed_at = null; queue null; ledger revenue to client_hold (B2B) or customer_funds (B2C), total_price; event reopened (data.reason); webhook STATUS 1; audit. Offered for both channels (lib/actions.ts:70). dispatch_state: done to operator (status processing, queue null).

errors.when: order is not completed (mock ordersActionRoutes.ts:43-51, orders.test.ts)

endpoints.mapConflict: Mock reopen also moves cogs back to supplier_prepaid (ordersActions.ts:114-133) while its refund keeps cogs (136-158); the map defines refund = reopen + reject and the UI says a refund loses the supplier cost. Proposal: reopen reverses revenue only, and a later reply on that order must not book cogs a second time unless a new supplier charge happened.

endpoints.request: Body `{ code, comment? }`: code = result text (trimmed, required); comment optional, up to 200 chars. The field-error name is `code` (CompleteDialog maps it to its reply input, CompleteDialog.tsx:83). Several orders are completed through bulk-reply/apply instead.
endpoints.response: 204. Open order becomes completed: result_code/result_comment, completed_at, outbox dispatch cancelled if not sent, reserved inventory code becomes sold. B2B ledger complete: client_hold to revenue (total_price), plus supplier_prepaid to cogs (total_cost) only when a supplier executed it (map manual scenario step 8 books revenue only). B2C: b2c_deliver (customer_funds to revenue net; VAT stays in vat_payable). Events completed + settle; webhook STATUS 4; audit. Toast: '<price> settled to revenue'. dispatch_state becomes done (any open order that is not held), status completed.

endpoints.request: Body `{ decision: accept | refund, note? }` (note up to 140 chars, VerificationDialog.tsx:50).
endpoints.response: 204. Only a completed order whose verification_status is requested (queue verification). accept: verification_status accepted, charge stands, event verification (data.decision). refund: verification_status refunded and the same money as POST refund (revenue to client_wallet, cogs kept), status rejected, result_code = note or a default text, webhook STATUS 3. dispatch_state stays done: accept keeps status completed (verification_status accepted); refund gives status rejected (verification_status refunded).

errors.when: decision not accept|refund (field decision) or note too long
errors.ui: dialog error slot / under the note

endpoints.request: Body `{ items: [{ orderId, code }] }` from the paste preview's matched lines, or from bulk Complete with the reply's `{input}` already replaced per order in the browser (CompleteDialog.tsx:51-60). No comment. At most 500 items: more is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED errors[{field: items}] 'At most 500 orders per apply'.
endpoints.response: 200 `{ applied, failed: [{ orderId, title }] }`. Each item is an independent POST reply (own DB transaction, same checks and ledger); a refused item goes to `failed` with a readable reason, shown verbatim in the summary dialog. Per-item refusals never turn the call into a 4xx.

errors.when: items missing, empty, malformed or more than 500

endpoints.request: Body `{ text }`: the pasted lines as typed.
endpoints.response: 200 `{ lines: [{ line, raw, imei, code, orderId, status }] }`; line is 1-based over the pasted text, blank lines skipped. First token (split on whitespace, comma or semicolon) = input, the rest = code. status: invalid (no input or no code), not_found (no order with that input), not_open (only closed orders), ambiguous (several open orders), matched (orderId set). Match orders.imei with whitespace removed (mock handlers/orders.ts:50-63); only non-empty imei values can match, so a blank input never does. Changes nothing.

businessRules: Status = map Dhru codes pending 0, processing 1, completed 4, rejected 3 (orders slice statuses). Open = pending|processing (status.ts:14-16); state-changing actions on a closed order answer 409 ORDER_NOT_OPEN (mock ordersShared.ts:13-14), so double clicks are harmless (no Idempotency-Key is sent).

queue derivation (mock src/mocks/orders.ts:110-138, map scenarios manual/timeout): review = B2C order held by risk (dispatch_state held, risk_assessments review undecided); manual = status pending and dispatch_state manual (manual step 5); needs_attention = dispatch_state needs_attention (timeout step 8; status stays pending until a REFERENCEID, the mock uses processing, the UI renders both); verification = status completed and verification_status requested; pending = status pending and dispatch_state pending (waiting in the outbox); otherwise null. After accept the queue must become null although no supplier is involved. dispatch_state operator (accepted by staff), sent and done have queue null; the full dispatch_state transition table is in decision 025 (lead resolution orders-suppliers-11) and every action has a test of its resulting queue.

reviewReason is readable text per queue: manual 'Manual service: operator dispatch required' (src/mocks/orders.ts:59), verification 'The merchant asked for the result to be checked', needs_attention = the supplier error or timeout text, review = risk summary; stored in the review order_event data.reason.

pastSla=true (demo isBreach 11-state.js:64, mock handlers/orders.ts:19-22): open (pending|processing) and now - placed_at (= created_at) > services.sla_minutes, with no queue exclusion (B92 supersedes the demo's 'not in a review queue'); a service with a null or 0 SLA is never past SLA; one predicate shared with the dashboard and GET /admin/system/orders-health.

Ledger per action (map moneyEvents): placement = order (client_wallet to client_hold) or b2c_pay; reply = complete (cogs leg only when a supplier executed the order) or b2c_deliver; reject = reject or b2c_refund; refund = revenue to client_wallet (cogs kept); reopen = revenue back to client_hold/customer_funds; verification refund = refund; accept, notes, change-supplier, dispatch and an unfinished fetch move no money. Each posting goes through postTransaction with ref_type order, ref_id = order id and one idempotency key per transition (decision 024); the drawer reads GET /admin/ledger/transactions?refType=order&refId=<id> sorted createdAt asc (useLedgerTrail.ts:12-13); mock tx kinds order_settle, order_release, refund, adjustment (orders.test.ts:157-189).
Every staff action writes order_events and audit_logs (map manual step 8); every status change emits outbox order.status_changed with the whole order (EVENT row).

Supplier timeout: no automatic resend; the order waits in needs_attention with the balance still held (map timeout step 8, decision 020). The UI recommends Fetch when supplier_ref exists, else Retry (lib/actions.ts:44-71).
Refund route only for completed B2B orders; B2C is refunded via /admin/refunds (map row, M25). Reopen and refund need orders:reopen; other actions orders:update (map).

Held B2C orders (queue review) are decided only through POST /admin/risk/orders/:id/approve|refund (risk:decide, M28); the UI offers no order action on them, the server should refuse reply/reject/dispatch with 409 (proposal ORDER_HELD).

Inventory-backed services: reserve a code at placement (inventory_codes.status reserved, order_id), mark it sold on completion (result_code = the code), release it to available when the order is rejected before delivery; a delivered code never returns to stock (refund/reopen leave it sold).
A service with no active supplier link, or executionMode manual, puts new orders in the manual queue (dispatch_state manual) (useReplaceLinks.ts:29-31, map manual scenario).
Field lengths the server must accept: reject reason 120, reopen reason 140, note 500, reply comment 200, verification note 140 (component maxLength attributes).
orders.source values dhru | v1 | portal | store | admin (status.ts:129-138); service types lower case imei|server|remote|file (M21).
Register GET /admin/orders/export (and other static sub-routes) before GET /admin/orders/:id (handlers/orders.ts:1-3).

Main input (lead resolution orders-suppliers-2): orders.imei is the order's main input whatever the service type (IMEI, the first required service field, or the uploaded file name), written by one shared helper at every placement; it is sent as an empty string when the column is NULL (erased or absent), and the bulk-reply preview never matches an empty input.

B117(6) scope (lead resolution orders-suppliers-12): the rule 'never fail over to a link costlier than the order's charged price' applies to automatic failover by the dispatch job only (the order goes to needs_attention); a staff change-supplier is an explicit human choice, allowed to a costlier link (unit_cost and total_cost are refreshed, the supplier_changed event records costAbovePrice), and the following staff dispatch sends to the chosen supplier service as is.

questions.question: Could POST /admin/orders/:id/change-supplier take `dispatch: true` so a reroute is one atomic call? (PROGRESS.md:252)
questions.proposedAnswer: Yes: optional `dispatch: true` changes the supplier and enqueues the dispatch in one transaction; without it the route keeps today's behaviour so the console's two-call flow still works.
questions.basis: map row POST /admin/orders/:id/change-supplier; M26; useBulkSend.ts:20-35

questions.question: Could the list sort by SLA urgency, the demo's default order? (PROGRESS.md:252)
questions.proposedAnswer: Not needed now: the console only sends createdAt, totalPrice or status (filters.ts:89). Later the server could add `_sort=slaDueAt` (created_at + sla minutes) as an indexed expression; the UI would need a small change to offer it.
questions.basis: M22; filters.ts:89-99; demo 41-p-orders.js

questions.question: The order DTO fields queue, reviewReason, channel and attempts have no columns. Derive or store them?
questions.proposedAnswer: Derive in the admin read model: queue from status + dispatch_state + verification_status + risk hold, reviewReason from the latest review order_event, channel from client_id/customer_id, attempts from dispatch/retry events. No new columns.
questions.basis: orders slice columns; scenarios manual and timeout; src/mocks/orders.ts:110-138

questions.question: Which status does an order have while it waits in needs_attention after a supplier timeout?
questions.proposedAnswer: Keep the Dhru status it had: pending (STATUS 0) when no REFERENCEID was received, processing when the timeout happened while polling; only dispatch_state changes. The console derives its words from queue, so both render.
questions.basis: map timeout scenario (step 8 sets dispatch, not status; track pending to processing); status.ts:28-34

questions.question: What does pastSla=true include? System health links needs_attention + pastSla (M230), but the demo excludes review queues.
questions.proposedAnswer: Follow the demo for /admin/orders: open, not in a review queue, older than the service SLA. Then the System health needs_attention link lists nothing; better change that link to queue=needs_attention without pastSla.
questions.basis: demo 11-state.js:64 isBreach; mock handlers/orders.ts:19-22; M230

questions.question: What does reopen do to the ledger, and is the supplier cost reversed?
questions.proposedAnswer: Reverse revenue only (revenue to client_hold, or customer_funds for B2C); cogs stays because the supplier already consumed the credit. A later reply posts hold to revenue without a second cogs leg unless a new supplier charge happened.
questions.basis: map row refund = reopen then reject; OrderFooter.tsx:140-141 copy; ordersActions.ts:114-158

questions.question: What does reject do for a B2C (storefront) order?
questions.proposedAnswer: A full refund before delivery as scenario b2c-refund: refunds row (method original, gross incl. VAT), gateway refund, ledger customer_funds + vat_payable to gateway_clearing, outbox dispatch cancelled, order rejected, all in one transaction.
questions.basis: scenario b2c-refund steps 3-4; moneyEvent b2c_refund; RejectDialog copy 'customers to their card'; ordersActions.ts:77-111

questions.question: A completed B2C order can be reopened from the drawer; may a later reject refund the card at once, bypassing /admin/refunds approval?
questions.proposedAnswer: Proposal: no. Reject on a B2C order that was delivered before answers 409 USE_REFUNDS, so post-delivery refunds always go through /admin/refunds (refunds:approve).
questions.basis: map row POST /admin/orders/:id/refund (storefront orders refunded from /admin/refunds); lib/actions.ts:70 offers reopen for both channels

questions.question: change-supplier sends a supplier id, but orders store supplier_service_id. How is the supplier service chosen?
questions.proposedAnswer: Use the order service's service_supplier_links row whose supplier service belongs to that supplier (active, lowest priority); refuse with 422 errors[{field: supplierId}] when the service has no link to that supplier. Optionally also accept supplierServiceId.
questions.basis: orders/suppliers tables; RetryMenu.tsx:30-37 offers every enabled supplier

questions.question: Is dispatch synchronous (supplier answered) or queued when the route returns?
questions.proposedAnswer: Queued: set dispatch_state pending, enqueue supplier-dispatch and answer 204; the worker sets processing on REFERENCEID. The console's 'Status is now Processing' toast is optimistic; it refetches the order anyway.
questions.basis: decision 020; map scenario dispatch steps; useOrderMutations.ts:139-150

questions.question: Which values does verification_status take and who sets requested?
questions.proposedAnswer: none | requested | accepted | refunded. POST /v1/orders/:id/verify and /client/orders/:id/verify set requested on a completed order within services.verify_window_h when allow_verify is true; the admin decision sets accepted or refunded.
questions.basis: map v1/client verify rows; services.allow_verify, verify_window_h; map order example verification none; ordersActions.ts:161-180

businessRules: Floor = effective cost (B117) + minProfit; minProfit = the service's own min_profit when set, else the min_profit (> 0) of the first matching rule in resolver order (rule 3; group-null rules only when there is no merchant), else max(round(6% x effective cost, 2), 0.02) (demo 10-data.js:215, FloorPolicy.tsx:8-10). A PATCH basePrice under the floor is refused with 422 on basePrice (demo setPrice, serviceRoutes.ts:145-155); orders always pay max(resolved price, floor) with clamped=true (map: selling below the minimum price is blocked).
Bulk price apply saves prices under the floor and reports their count (useBulkPrice.ts:25-29); the floor is still enforced at order time.

Resolver (one catalog PriceResolver used by resolve, orders, price lists and the client/group price checks; lead resolution catalog-4): (1) step client: service_client_prices wins; (2) step group: service_group_prices for the merchant's group wins when there is no client price; (3) step base: services.base_price, applied unless a client or group price fixed it; (4) the rule step (id 'category', kept for the console's fraction display; label 'Service rule' | 'Category rule' | 'Global rule' by the winning rule's scope): pick ONE rule that is_active, with starts_at null or <= now, ends_at null or > now, group_id null or the merchant's group and a matching target (service: target_id = service id; category: target_id = category id; global), ordered by scope (service, category, global), then priority asc, then group-specific before group-null, then id asc; unless fixed, p = p x (1 + s x percent/100) + s x fixed with s = +1 for margin and -1 for discount and promo; value = the signed fraction (after/before - 1, 4 dp) and the note names the rule and any fixed amount; (5) step discount: client_groups.discount_percent/100, applied unless fixed, then round half-up to 2 dp; (6) step rounding (id 'rounding', label 'Rounding'), emitted only when not fixed and the winning rule's rounding is not 'none': nearest_0.05 and nearest_0.10 round half-up to that step, ends_99 = floor(p) + 0.99; its value and after are the rounded price; rawPrice is the price after step 6; (7) floor clamp: floor = effective cost + minProfit, price = max(rawPrice, floor), clamped = true when raised. minProfit = services.min_profit when not null, else the min_profit of the first rule in the step-4 order (same filters) with min_profit > 0, else max(round(6% x effective cost, 2), 0.02). Without a merchant (admin rows, belowFloor, PATCH basePrice, bulk) only group_id-null rules match. otherGroups = every b2b group, no client override. Fixed (client or group) prices skip steps 4 to 6, as in the demo (demo resolveWith, mock pricing.ts:63-141).

Rule direction comes from kind: margin adds, discount and promo subtract; percent and fixed are >= 0 with at least one > 0 (ruleRoutes.ts:46-75); a promo applies only between startsAt and endsAt; rule changes affect new orders only.

Categories: allowed_group_ids empty = visible to every group (M94); no parent category; category type is one of the four service types; a service's type equals its category's type (composite FK services (category_id, type) to service_categories (id, type)) and a category with live services cannot change type (422 on type); a category name is unique within its type, case-insensitive.

Delete guards: category with services 409 CATEGORY_IN_USE; a service with orders, links, listings or other references is archived (archived_at set, status disabled, its rules inactive), otherwise deleted, both 204 (SERVICE_IN_USE is retired); a category is deleted only when no service row, live or archived, references it (its category-scope rules are deleted with it), otherwise 409 CATEGORY_IN_USE; deleting a group removes its group prices and rules (client-groups delete); rules delete freely.
Service code is unique case-insensitive: 409 CODE_TAKEN with errors[{field: code}] on create and edit.
Replace-all PUTs (fields, options, group-prices) delete and insert in one transaction and answer the saved list in order.

Inventory: codes encrypted (code_enc), deduplicated globally on a keyed hash, never returned in clear or logged; the list shows the last four characters; void affects only available codes (reserved belong to open orders, sold were delivered).

A disabled service is hidden from merchants (imeiservicelist) while its open orders continue; executionMode manual sends new orders to the manual queue (types/service.ts ServiceStatus/ExecutionMode JSDoc, map manual scenario).
Money maths in decimal: prices rounded half-up to 2 decimals at the named points (mock round), emitted as 4-dp strings (decision 011); marginPct and percent are decimal strings.

Lookups read by these screens (merchants feature routes, no @route here): GET /admin/client-groups?_start=0&_end=200&_sort=sort&_order=asc (groups:read; rows need kind incl. b2c_retail and discountPercent, optional merchantCount) and GET /admin/clients?_start=0&_end=200&_sort=name&_order=asc (clients:read; optional group join) (api/lookups.ts).
Every catalog and pricing write is audit-logged (map: any admin mutation goes to audit_logs).
Register POST /admin/services/bulk-price/* (and GET /admin/pricing/resolve) so they never fall into /admin/services/:id handlers (mocks/index.ts:16-17).

Group prices are floor-checked on save (lead resolution catalog-12, next to rule 1): PUT /admin/services/:id/group-prices refuses a b2b row under that group's floor (effective cost + the group's minProfit) and the b2c_retail row under max(round(base_price x 1.10, 2), floor), as 422 on prices.N.price; the whole set is validated, unchanged rows included; bulk price apply keeps its accepted exception (rule 2).

problem+json errors[] items {field, message} with dotted paths (fields.0.key, prices.1.price, options.3.value) land on form inputs (src/lib/api/errors.ts:125-163, applyServerErrors); field names must equal body keys, the dialogs list them (CompleteDialog.tsx:83 aliases code to reply, ServiceFormDialog.tsx:81, suppliers lib/input.ts:21-32); unknown fields still show in the dialog's error slot.

Static sub-routes must win over :id routes: GET /admin/orders/export vs /admin/orders/:id (src/mocks/handlers/orders.ts:1-3), POST /admin/services/bulk-price/* vs /admin/services/:id (src/features/services/mocks/index.ts:16-17); :id params are integers (decision 010).

Decimal inputs are not always 4-dp padded: bulk change.value is signed with 0-4 decimals ('5', '-0.25', src/features/services/lib/bulk.ts:29) while rule percent/fixed/minProfit are padded ('0.0000', ruleForm.ts:67). Accept 0-4 decimals with an optional minus sign where signed, and always emit 4-dp strings (decision 011).

Ratios are JSON numbers 0-100 on suppliers and the report (successRate1h, rejectionRate) but decimal strings on services and rules (marginPct, percent) (suppliers types/index.ts, services types/service.ts and types/pricing.ts); keep each field's type as typed.

Admin actions send no Idempotency-Key (no header in src/features/*/api): reply, reject, refund, verification and bulk-reply/apply must be safe against double submit through state checks (409) plus ledger idempotency keys (decision 024).

GET /admin/files/:id is a top-level navigation in a new tab carrying only cookies (src/features/orders/components/OrderResult.tsx:26-31): the session cookie must travel on cross-subdomain top-level GETs (SameSite=Lax) and the route answers 302 to a signed URL without a CSRF check.
Rule dates are ISO instants computed from the admin's local day bounds (src/features/services/lib/ruleForm.ts:58-67): store them as timestamptz, never truncate to a date.

Bulk work is sequential single calls (src/features/orders/lib/bulk.ts:20-44, src/features/suppliers/lib/reroute.ts): admin rate limits must tolerate about 200 sequential POSTs from one session; a 401 stops the run.
